title: Nilpotence does not guarantee an Anosov lattice automorphism
notes: The parenthesis states that such automorphisms exist if and only if the Lie algebra is nilpotent.
statement: Nilpotence alone is not sufficient. For the three-dimensional Heisenberg group with its standard lattice, a lattice-preserving automorphism induces \(B\in GL(2,\mathbb Z)\) on the abelianization and acts on the one-dimensional center by \(\det B=\pm1\). Hence its derivative always has an eigenvalue of modulus one and cannot define an Anosov automorphism. The existence of an appropriate lattice-preserving hyperbolic automorphism is an additional arithmetic and algebraic condition.
reconstruction: This is an editorial counterexample, with its symbolic bracket calculation included in the fragment's checks.
fate: The restricted nature of algebraic examples is consistent with \citet[\S2]{spatzier2016rigidity}. The explicit Heisenberg bracket calculation is supplied here as a direct counterexample to the notebook's converse; no general classification of Anosov Lie algebras is claimed.

title: Are all Anosov diffeomorphisms algebraic up to conjugacy?
notes: The main problem is \ru{топ. подобность алгебраич.}; small perturbations are already handled by Anosov's theorem.
statement: Is every Anosov diffeomorphism of a compact connected manifold topologically conjugate to an affine Anosov automorphism of an infranilmanifold? The distinction between determining the underlying manifold and conjugating its dynamics is essential. Smooth conjugacy is a stronger assertion and is not the question recorded here.
fate: This repeats 1966-94.4 and reuses GP-1966-01. \citet[Conjecture 2.3 and Theorem 2.4]{spatzier2016rigidity} states the precise conjecture and the Franks--Manning result on infranilmanifolds. \citet[\S2]{damjanovic2026symmetries} still describes algebraicity of general Anosov dynamics as conjectural. Sinai's two-torus case appears as Theorem 5.2 of \citet{sinai1968markov}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the general classification remains open. The two-torus case and the Franks--Manning classification when the manifold is already an infranilmanifold are established; structural stability solves only a neighborhood of a known example.
worth: Further work is worthwhile on explicit manifold classes or additional dynamical hypotheses, since these address the remaining global classification rather than reproving local structural stability.

title: Hyperbolicity on the nonwandering set: an incomplete quantifier
notes: The manifold is split into wandering and nonwandering points, and the \(U\)-condition is asserted on the latter, with a margin note saying this too is a hypothesis.
statement: For a homeomorphism, a point is nonwandering when every neighborhood meets one of its positive iterates; its complement is the wandering set. It is false that the nonwandering set of every smooth diffeomorphism is hyperbolic: the identity is an immediate counterexample. A density or genericity conjecture would require a topology, a class of systems, and an approximation quantifier, none of which is stated here.
fate: The terminology belongs to the hyperbolic-dynamics programme surveyed by \citet{smale1967dynamical}, but this fragment does not determine which conjecture was intended. It must not be automatically identified with the earlier Axiom A or periodic-density questions merely because the words nonwandering and hyperbolic occur.
present_status: As of November 2026, the literal universal assertion is false and the intended qualified conjecture cannot be uniquely recovered. No new problem-index entry is assigned.

title: Absolute continuity of holonomy
notes: The canonical map between nearby stable plaques, obtained along unstable plaques, need not be smooth but is absolutely continuous; natural measures are said to be carried into one another.
statement: For a \(C^{1+\alpha}\) Anosov diffeomorphism, \(\alpha>0\), stable and unstable holonomies between appropriate smooth transverse plaques are absolutely continuous with respect to the induced Riemannian volume classes. Thus a null set is carried to a null set in both directions. This does not assert equality of the two Riemannian volume measures or differentiability of the holonomy.
reconstruction: The modern \(C^{1+\alpha}\) regularity condition and preservation of measure classes, rather than measure values, are explicit.
fate: \citet[\S1, p.65]{sinai1968markov} states exactly the equivalence of the induced volume classes, attributing the established argument to Anosov and noting that a smooth invariant global measure is not required. The notebook's warning about lack of smoothness is substantive.

title: Rectangles from the local product structure
notes: A parallelogram consists of stable and unstable leaf pieces, canonically identified within each family. Its boundary splits into expanding and contracting parts; finitely many such pieces cover the manifold with disjoint interiors.
statement: A sufficiently small rectangle is a set closed under the local bracket \([x,y]=W^s_{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\cap W^u_{\mathrm{loc}}(y)\), with a product description by stable and unstable plaques. A rectangular partition has finitely many such closed pieces, covers the manifold, and has pairwise disjoint interiors. Its two boundary types come from the boundaries in the two local-product factors. In higher dimensions these rectangles need not be Euclidean polyhedra.

fate: This is \citet[\S1, Definitions 1.1--1.2]{sinai1968markov}; the published admissibility conditions also control plaque-boundary measure. The schematic figures in the notebook do not assert piecewise linear boundaries.

title: Markov boundary inclusions
notes: The partition is Markov when, for some \(m>0\), \(\Gamma_p(T^{-m}\alpha)\subset\Gamma_p(\alpha)\) and \(\Gamma_c(T^m\alpha)\subset\Gamma_c(\alpha)\).

In the usual one-step formulation, if \(x\in\operatorname{int}R_i\) and \(Tx\in\operatorname{int}R_j\), then \(T(W^s(x,R_i))\subset W^s(Tx,R_j)\) and \(T(W^u(x,R_i))\supset W^u(Tx,R_j)\). title: Coding by admissible itineraries

title: Primitivity and density of the invariant leaves
notes: A strictly positive power of \(\Pi\) is required, and this is said to be equivalent to density of every stable and unstable leaf.
statement: Within the Markov coding of a connected Anosov system, the mixing case has a primitive transition matrix. Sinai's theorem identifies this condition with density of every stable and every unstable leaf. His word transitive in this part of the paper is defined by the positive-power matrix condition, which is stronger than mere irreducibility of a general finite matrix. title: Holonomy-invariant measures on stable and unstable leaves
notes: Each stable leaf has a sigma-finite measure invariant under canonical holonomy, with \(\lambda_c(TA)=h\lambda_c(A)\), \(h<1\), an algebraic number. The finite-dimensional construction is \(h^{-1}\vec\lambda=\Pi\vec\lambda\).
statement: For the mixing Anosov system under discussion, there are nonzero locally finite, hence sigma-finite, stable-leaf measures invariant under unstable holonomy, with \(\mu^s(TA)=\lambda^{-1}\mu^s(A)\), where \(\lambda>1\) is the Perron eigenvalue of a one-step Markov matrix. The analogous unstable-leaf measures scale by \(\lambda\) under \(T\). Initial plaque masses satisfy the appropriate Perron eigenvector equation, and subdivision extends them to the leaves. Thus the scaling factors are algebraic. They need not be equivalent to Riemannian leaf volume.
reconstruction: The notebook's \(h\) is \(\lambda^{-1}\), a scaling factor rather than entropy. The separate unstable family and singularity possibility are made explicit.
fate: This is exactly \citet[\S5, Theorem 5.1, pp.84--86]{sinai1968markov}; it is a general statement in that mixing setting, preceding the two-torus specialization in Theorem 5.2. For linear toral examples the leaf measures arise from Haar measure, as the notebook remarks.

title: An invariant measure with a finite Markov model
notes: As a corollary there is an invariant measure for which \(T\) is a finite Markov chain. The illustrated construction then specializes to dimension two.
statement: For a mixing finite Markov coding, the Parry probability pushes forward to an invariant probability. When the coding boundaries have zero measure, the resulting system is isomorphic modulo zero to the finite-state stationary Markov shift. For a hyperbolic toral automorphism, Haar probability has exactly this Markov property and is the maximal-entropy measure. For nonlinear dynamics the constructed maximal-entropy measure need not be smooth volume or the measure with absolutely continuous unstable conditionals.

fate: \citet[Theorem 5.4 and its proof]{sinai1968markov} proves the Haar/Markov assertion for every hyperbolic toral automorphism; Theorem 5.1 supplies the leaf-measure construction used in the surrounding talk. The boundary-null and measure-class distinctions explain what is required when the notebook states its broader corollary without qualifications.

title: Entropy, the Perron root, and the repeated metric classification
notes: The page first gives \(h(T)=\log\lambda\), then writes \(h(T)=\lambda\), and returns to metric isomorphism through the standard symbolic model.
statement: For a hyperbolic two-torus automorphism, Haar entropy is \(\log\rho(A)\). More generally, in the mixing Anosov Markov construction, \(h_{\mathrm{top}}(T)=\log\lambda\), where \(\lambda\) is the Perron root and the stable-leaf scaling factor is \(\lambda^{-1}\). The equality \(h(T)=\lambda\) on the next notebook line omits the logarithm if the same symbol \(\lambda\) is intended. title: The two-rectangle torus partition and its connected refinement
notes: Two parallelograms have sides along eigenlines through zero. The coarse itinerary can contain many points. Intersections \(V_i\cap TV_j\) are refined into connected components in four groups of sizes \(p,q,r,s\); one of the four displayed intersections is repeated.
statement: For a real hyperbolic two-torus automorphism, a suitable two-rectangle partition is built from segments in its stable and unstable eigendirections. The component refinement of all four intersections \(V_i\cap TV_j\), \(i,j\in\{1,2\}\), gives a generating Markov partition with the four-block transition structure in 1967-138.9.
